content: Triplegia is a medical condition characterized by paralysis affecting three limbs. This condition is commonly associated with cerebral palsy, although it can also result from other medical conditions, such as a stroke. Additionally, triplegia has been observed in cases where increased intracranial pressure, often linked to hydrocephalus caused by traumatic brain injury, is present. An individual with triplegia is referred to as a triplegic. In the context of cerebral palsy, triplegia is often considered a combination of hemiplegia and diplegia. Alternatively, it may be a form of quadriplegia with significantly reduced involvement of one limb. In most cases, both legs and one arm are affected, although it is also possible for both arms and one leg to be involved. For children with triplegia, resources designed for those with quadriplegia are generally the most beneficial. A related condition is triparesis, in which the patient experiences paresis, or severe weakness, in three limbs. Unlike triplegia, the affected limbs in triparesis are not completely paralyzed but are significantly weakened.
